title: Exponential Smoothing / ETS
interviewAnswer: Exponential smoothing builds forecasts from recursively updated level, trend and seasonality components, giving more weight to recent observations. ETS models are excellent business-forecasting baselines, especially when patterns are smooth and recurring.
why: ETS often performs extremely well on operational forecasting with little tuning and has an intuitive decomposition for stakeholders.
intuition: Instead of fitting one global regression line, keep updating a compact state of “where the series is now, where it is moving, and what season we are in.”
deepDive: Simple exponential smoothing models level only; Holt adds trend; Holt-Winters adds seasonality. Additive vs multiplicative components depend on whether seasonal amplitude stays constant or grows with the level.
workedExample: If monthly demand has a stable upward trend and December is consistently +20 units, additive seasonal ETS is natural. If the December uplift is about +20%, multiplicative seasonality may fit better.
commonMistakes: Assuming exponential smoothing is just a moving average.
Using multiplicative seasonality when zeros/negative values make it inappropriate.
production: ETS is lightweight and reliable for batch forecasting, and is a strong champion model to compare with more expensive approaches.

lab.useIt:
from statsmodels.tsa.holtwinters import ExponentialSmoothing
m=ExponentialSmoothing(y,trend='add',seasonal='add',seasonal_periods=12).fit()
f=m.forecast(12)
print(f)
lab.shipIt: Keep a reproducible backtest by horizon; retrain only after the newest complete observations and compare against seasonal-naive before deployment.
